name: Swedish
script: Latin with extra letters: å, ä, ö; left to right
basis: Topics and grammar of Rivstart A1+A2, units 1-6, as taught in a 30-week Level 1 course
src: BHASVIC (Brighton): Swedish Level 1 course outline, Rivstart A1+A2 textbook units 1-6, themes and grammar topics
note: The outline lists Rivstart's themes and grammar (present, imperative, infinitive, modal + infinitive, pronouns, question words, word order, numbers, nouns indefinite / definite / plural, indefinite adjectives, frequency adverbs, tycker om, an introduction to the past) but not their order. The lesson order, the two sounds lessons, possessives, directions and the titles are common course practice and my own judgment.
hardest: Long vs short vowels and the vowels å, ä, ö, u, y
The sj- and tj- sounds, and k / g that soften before e, i, y, ä, ö
en or ett for each noun, and the definite ending (bilen, huset)
Verb in second place, and where inte goes

items: Vowels: long and short, å, ä, ö, u, y
Tricky sounds: sj-, tj-, soft k and g, and the two word tones
Introducing yourself: Jag heter…, Jag kommer från…
Numbers and prices: Vad kostar det?
Pronouns: jag, du, han, hon, vi, ni, de
Present tense in -r: jag bor, han talar
Verb in second place: Idag jobbar jag
Questions: vad, var, vem, när, hur, and yes/no questions
inte: negation and where it goes
en and ett: the two genders
Telling the time: halv tre, kvart över
Modal verbs + infinitive: vill, kan, måste, ska
At the café: Kan jag få en kaffe?, and fika
Adjectives: en stor bil, ett stort hus, stora hus
Family and daily routine: ofta, alltid, aldrig
Likes and hobbies: tycker om, gillar
Infinitive with att: Jag tycker om att läsa
Directions: till höger, till vänster, rakt fram
Past tense: jag pratade, jag var, jag hade
